packages.title: ONS UK Environmental Accounts: 2026 — scope and status QA
facts: ONS released UK Environmental Accounts: 2026 on 5 June 2026.
The bulletin estimates 478 million tonnes CO2e of UK greenhouse-gas emissions on a residence basis in 2024.
Residence-basis estimates cover UK residents and UK-registered businesses wherever they operate, while excluding foreign visitors and foreign businesses in the UK.
The bulletin combines emissions and direct-energy-use statistics but these accounting measures are not parcel-level observations.
No parcel greenhouse-gas value is inferred from the national environmental accounts.

packages.title: ONS Atmospheric emissions: greenhouse gases by industry and gas — scope and status QA
facts: The ONS dataset was released on 5 June 2026 and covers UK greenhouse-gas emissions from 1990 to 2024.
It reports carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, HFCs, PFCs, sulphur hexafluoride, nitrogen trifluoride and total greenhouse-gas emissions.
Industry detail uses SIC 2007 groups across roughly 130 categories.
Current and provisional dataset editions are separate and their revision status must be preserved.
Industry-account emissions are not direct measurements for individual land parcels.

packages.title: ONS Measuring UK greenhouse gas emissions — scope and status QA
facts: ONS revised its greenhouse-gas measurement methodology page on 7 July 2026.
The methodology distinguishes territorial, residence or production, and footprint or consumption measures.
It states an estimated 367 MtCO2e for UK territorial emissions in 2025.
It states a provisional 478 MtCO2e for UK production emissions in 2024.
Accounting-basis totals must not be converted into parcel-level emissions without a separate parcel-binding method.

packages.title: ONS Energy use: renewable and waste sources — scope and status QA
facts: The ONS dataset was released on 5 June 2026.
It covers UK energy use from renewable and waste sources from 1990 to 2024.
The dataset distinguishes energy sources such as hydroelectric, wind, wave and solar and reports industry groupings.
Energy use is an activity measure and is not itself an avoided-greenhouse-gas measurement.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from renewable or waste energy use.

packages.title: ONS Energy use: by industry, source and fuel — scope and status QA
facts: The ONS dataset was released on 5 June 2026 and covers 1990 to 2024.
It provides UK energy use by around 130 SIC industry groups, around 80 activity sources and around 20 fuels.
Examples of activity sources include industrial combustion, domestic combustion, aircraft and road transport.
Fuel-use activity must remain distinct from greenhouse-gas emissions unless an explicit conversion model is applied.
No property-level emissions observation is created from the energy-use table.

packages.title: DfT Transport and environment statistics: 2024 — scope and status QA
facts: DfT published Transport and environment statistics: 2024 on 14 July 2026.
The release reports 110.4 MtCO2e from domestic transport in 2024.
It reports domestic transport as 30% of total UK domestic greenhouse-gas emissions in 2024.
The release also reports transport shares of NOx, PM2.5 and PM10 emissions.
National transport emissions by mode are not parcel greenhouse-gas measurements.

packages.title: DfT Transport energy and environment data tables (ENV) — scope and status QA
facts: DfT last updated the ENV transport energy and environment tables on 14 July 2026.
The tables include fuel consumption, greenhouse-gas emissions, pollutants and emissions from journeys.
Coverage periods differ between tables and must be retained when comparing values.
The tables draw on the most recently available data sources and should not be treated as a single common-vintage dataset.

packages.title: DfT Transport Statistics Geography Portal: June 2026 — scope and status QA
facts: DfT published the June 2026 Transport Statistics Geography Portal update on 24 June 2026.
The portal presents existing published official transport statistics in geographic form.
